audit: AX211 AirportItlwm forensic source audit (Sequoia 15.8.2 / MSI Modern 14 C12MO)
evidence_context: Source-only audit: remote runtime access blocked (see 23-environment-access.md). Classifications are source-evidence based; runtime confirmation pending via tools/ diagnostic kit.

findings.title: PCI device support table: 19 IDs, AX211 correctly present as So-family
findings.evidence: iwx_devices[] ItlIwx.cpp:12377-12406 (19 entries); trans cfgs 12175-12227; iwl_dev_info_table 12765-13338 (~230 entries); iwx_match 13340-13346; attach matching 13550-13643. 0x51F0 -> iwl_so_long_latency_trans_cfg (family AX210/gen3) -> iwlax211_2ax_cfg_so_gf_a0 -> fw iwlwifi-so-a0-gf-a0-68.ucode (12243-12249).
findings.analysis: AX211 on 0x51F0 lands on the correct gen3 config and firmware; the 19 driver-table IDs exactly equal the 19 Info.plist IOPCIMatch IDs (AUDIT-1 section 6). Verified trace for the audit target (0x51F0 + GF RFID) is correct.
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a - validated from source; CI verify step greps the 5 AX211-family PCI IDs.

findings.title: Four advertised PCI IDs can never load firmware (blobs not embedded)
findings.evidence: Info.plist IOPCIMatch includes 0x2720/0x2726/0x2729/0x7E40 whose cfgs reference firmware absent from itlwm/firmware/: QuQnj-*-48 (12504-12516, 12668-12680), SoSnj-*-63 (12295-12315), ma-a0-*-63 (12317-12357, 13181-13206). iwx_read_firmware fails getFWDescByName==NULL (1461-1466) -> iwx_preinit fail5 (13780-13782) -> attach returns false.
findings.analysis: On those machines the kext matches the PCI device (IOProbeScore 2000) then fails firmware load, leaving Wi-Fi dead and potentially blocking a competing driver. Harmless to the AX211 target but a correctness defect and prime Tier-2 reduction target.
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a - source-confirmed; CI strings check shows those 11 names present in the binary only as device-table .fwname references, never embedded.

findings.title: dev_info matching loop never breaks: last match wins instead of first match
findings.evidence: 13560-13594: for-loop over iwl_dev_info_table sets sc->sc_cfg on every match with no break; later less-specific wildcard entries overwrite sc->sc_cfg. Linux pcie.c and OpenBSD if_iwx.c stop at the first (most specific) match. Inherited verbatim from upstream 7204c69 (same lines).
findings.analysis: AX211 is accidentally correct (0x51F0+GF lands on iwlax211_2ax_cfg_so_gf_a0 regardless), but Qu-family firmware selection depends on table ordering rather than specificity; any future table edit can silently change which ucode a laptop loads.
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a - source-level; runtime effect only on non-AX211 devices.

findings.title: Qu C0 / QuZ step-fixup hack compares raw sc_hw_rev against a type-constant
findings.evidence: 13611: sc->sc_hw_rev == CSR_HW_REV_TYPE_QU_C0 - should be CSR_HW_REV_TYPE(sc->sc_hw_rev) == ... (constant 0x338 includes reserved positions; raw register also carries step bits). Same pattern at 13621 (QuZ); fixup body 13612-1367 is effectively dead code.
findings.analysis: The fixup is effectively dead - equality on the raw value almost never holds. Mitigated in practice by generic mac_step dev_info entries (DRV-IWX-003). Qu-family only; no AX211 impact.
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a - dead code confirmed by reading.

findings.title: MSI-X fully implemented but hard-disabled (if (0)) - single-vector MSI only
findings.evidence: 13483-13489: if (0) { sc->sc_msix = 1; ... } else if (pci_intr_map_msi(...)). Full MSIX implementation retained: iwx_conf_msix_hw 3127-3212 (~85 lines), iwx_intr_msix 12059-12146, msix branches 2811-2920 - all dead.
findings.analysis: Functional but single-interrupt: RX, TX completions, ALIVE, RFKILL and errors share one vector and one workloop serialization point (latency under load). Dead MSIX code is a Tier-2 removal candidate; not an AX211-specific regression.
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a on target (single-vector by design); could enumerate interrupt sources via IORegistry in the macOS diagnostics kit (optional).

findings.title: Firmware selection chain and the 15 embedded blobs - AX211 needs only 2
findings.evidence: fwname chosen at 13638; blob resolved by name from zlib fwList[] (1461-1469, FwData.h:33-44); .pnvm companion derived by string surgery (2072-2081); PNVM section applied only if SKU-id + mac_type/rf_id match (2130-2139). Embedded set: 15 files, 16,700,476 raw bytes (12 .ucode + 3 .pnvm, all API-68 core66_LinADLPV::01d30b0c).
findings.analysis: For 0x51F0 the only reachable firmwares are so-a0-gf-a0-68 (+.pnvm) for GF radios and so-a0-gf4-a0-68 (+.pnvm) for Killer AX411 subdevices; a strict AX211(0x51F0+GF) build needs 2 of 15 blobs (1,575,620 B = 9.4%) - the other 13 serve only non-target DIDs (reduction opportunity, cross-ref REPO-002).
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a - verified at binary level by CI strings check (CI-003).

findings.title: Firmware decompression uses compressed_size*4 output-buffer heuristic; inflate return ignored
findings.evidence: 1467-1469: fw_rawsize = len*4; uncompressFirmware return value not checked (FwData.h:46-70 returns false on Z_BUF_ERROR leaving *destLen unchanged); same pattern for PNVM with *20 (2090-2092).
findings.analysis: If a future ucode inflates to >4x compressed size, inflate fails silently and the TLV parser walks a partially-initialized heap buffer; the magic check (1481-1487) likely rejects it (EINVAL), so blast radius is a failed load rather than corruption. Heuristic holds with current API-68 blobs.
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a - bounded by compressed-size ratios of the 15 blobs (open question 7); no runtime path on target.

findings.title: PNVM load flow: dead goto, doorbell kicked even when read failed, 2 s gate-held wait
findings.evidence: iwx_load_pnvm 2154-2184: goto out is a no-op (both paths fall into out:); when iwx_read_pnvm fails (SKU mismatch, 2014-2026 returns -ENOENT) the doorbell is still rung and iwx_wait_notification blocks up to 2000 ms; error propagates via iwx_load_ucode_wait_alive (5041-5043) as hard failure -> stop/retry loop 10779-10791.
findings.analysis: Every boot on hardware whose fused SKU-id mismatches a PNVM section burns a 2-second timeout inside the gated bring-up path; plausible contributor to slow/unreliable interface bring-up. Linux uses 250 ms + fail-flag short-circuit (LINUX-014), evidencing this is a defect, not a firmware requirement.
findings.runtime_confirmation: macOS diagnostics kit: check 08-kernel-log for 'PNVM complete notification' vs timeout/EWOULDBLOCK at each boot and wake (open question 2).

findings.title: Synchronous command path: 1 s sleep timeout leaks the ring slot if firmware never answers
findings.evidence: iwx_send_cmd 6510-6728; sync completion 6695-6706 commandSleep 1 s THREAD_UNINT; on THREAD_TIMED_OUT -> EWOULDBLOCK; ring->queued++/CMD_PENDING (6688-6691) only undone by iwx_cmd_done (6799-6829) or iwx_reset_tx_ring (2736-2776); admission check 6555-6557 returns ENOSPC when ring full or slot pending; cmd ring = 128 slots gen3.
findings.analysis: If firmware wedges without raising SW_ERR/HW_ERR, every timed-out command permanently consumes one of the 128 cmd-ring slots; after enough failures iwx_send_cmd returns ENOSPC for all commands and state-machine errors trigger full reinit via init_task (10248-10254) - matches association/scan failure loops in field reports. Recovery ultimately depends on the 15 s TX watchdog (10914, 11021-11057). [confidence normalized from report Medium-High]
findings.runtime_confirmation: macOS diagnostics kit: 08-kernel-log across sleep/wake cycles - watch for command timeouts/ENOSPC and reinit sequences.

findings.title: TX data path: one shared 1024-slot queue for non-aggregated traffic; gen3 aggregation capped to 256 slots (acknowledged freeze bug)
findings.evidence: Queue selection iwx_tx 6996-7014: default qid=first_data_qid (queue 2 MGMT, iwx_enable_mgmt_queue 9054-9075); per-TID queues only when ba_state==AGREED. iwx_alloc_tx_ring 2661-2672: gen3 non-cmd rings would be 1024 slots but iwx_tvqm_alloc_txq 3501-3506 caps gen3 to 256 via #ifdef notyet with author TODO: 'TfDs count larger than 256 would trigger system freeze on macOS'. Backpressure: qfullmsk 7179-7182; _iwx_start_task 10860-10863 stops whole interface when any ring full; ac pinned EDCA_AC_BE XXX (10850).
findings.analysis: Until ADDBA completes, management and all 4 ACs contend on one ring (EAPOL starvation, cross-ref DRV-11D-011/018); the 256-TFD cap plus the unexplained 'system freeze' note means gen3 aggregation throughput is deliberately halved vs Linux (LINUX-011) and the underlying DMA issue is unresolved. [report: known and worked around]
findings.runtime_confirmation: macOS diagnostics kit: sleep/wake 3 cycles + speed test each (DRV-IWX-011 guided check); watch for freeze at >256 outstanding TFDs (needs controlled reproduction).

findings.title: TX aggregation teardown never releases firmware/driver queues - leak across BA cycles
findings.evidence: iwx_ampdu_tx_stop 4714-4729 in its entirety: sc_tid_data[tid].qid = IWX_INVALID_QUEUE; is_ht_tx_ba_agreements--. No IWX_SCD_QUEUE_CFG remove/disable, no iwx_free_tx_ring. Each ADDBA start allocates a fresh TVQM queue via iwx_tvqm_alloc_txq (3497-3526) -> iwx_tvqm_enable_txq (3528-3696); iwx_rm_sta (7646-7679) sends no queue removal.
findings.analysis: The firmware never learns the old queue is gone, so fwqid monotonically increases; after ~64 association/roam/sleep cycles TVQM allocation must fail, after which iwx_ba_task refuses ADDBA (4615-4618) and the link drops to non-aggregated throughput permanently until reboot. Credible mechanism for 'Wi-Fi degrades after sleep/wake or roaming'.
findings.runtime_confirmation: macOS diagnostics kit: sleep/wake 3 cycles + speed test each; log capture watching for 'Failed allocating TXQ' after >=60 reassociations (open question 1).

findings.title: Gen3 firmware-load error path leaks three DMA allocations
findings.evidence: iwx_ctxt_info_gen3_init 1157-1268: at 1255-1258 if (!iwx_nic_lock(sc)) return EBUSY; - returns without freeing sc->prph_scratch_dma, sc->prph_info_dma, sc->iml_dma (fail1/fail0 labels 1262-1267 bypassed); retry loop 10779-10791 overwrites the pointers and leaks again.
findings.analysis: Only reachable when the MAC-access handshake fails during load; leaks a few hundred KB per occurrence and leaves prph_scratch_dma.vaddr non-NULL; bounded by reinit frequency; contributes to long-uptime memory growth.
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a - source-confirmed; long-uptime wired-memory growth observable via macOS kit 09-power/vm stats.

findings.title: Hardware init sequence: correct and complete for So/AX211 (gen3 path)
findings.evidence: Full chain verified: iwx_attach 13441-13799 (PCIe caps, reg 0x40 clear, BAR0, MSI, ICT, gen3 ctxt_info 13648-13653, rings, taskqs); iwx_preinit 13348-13422 (first boot only, static attached); iwx_init_hw 10585-10718 (per up); gen3 iwx_ctxt_info_gen3_init 1157-1268 with UREG_CPU_INIT_RUN (1257); alive v4/v5 parsing 11550-11597 (v5 extracts sku_id[] for PNVM matching); AX211 branches (>= AX210 family, GEN3_UMAC_PRPH_OFFSET 2210-2235, 24-bit prph_msk 2186-2192) all correctly gated.
findings.analysis: The sequence matches iwlwifi's gen3 self-init flow (context-info + IML) closely; no defect found in the happy path.
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a - validated source-only; physical bring-up validated by owner (basic Wi-Fi works).

findings.title: Command allocation/queueing mechanics: TX ring 0, wide-header, narrow-group hack
findings.evidence: All commands via sc->txq[IWX_DQA_CMD_QUEUE]=0 (6521); per-slot response buffers (6567-6583 alloc, 11681 copy, ownership 6716-6718); Intel-inside remap of group-0 commands into LONG_GROUP for fw API>=50 (6585-6596) with inverse on RX (11478-11484, CMD_IS_NARROW); TFD TB0/TB1 split at 20 B (6662-6672); ring kick 6693; async never sleeps, WANT_RESP+async rejected (6558-6559); ENXIO/ENOSPC/EINVAL propagation (6545-6547, 6605-6610).
findings.analysis: Sound design; risk is concentrated in the timeout path (DRV-IWX-009) and in the per-slot response buffer being freed while a late response is in flight (handled by NULL check 11659-11663).
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a.

findings.title: RX path: ring, replenishment, dispatch table
findings.evidence: 512-entry RX ring, 4 KB buffers (5142-5194); gen3 16-byte transfer-desc free-list + used-ring (5124-5140, 2503-2535); iwx_notif_intr 11876-12004 (gen3 2-byte closed-idx 11885-11889, WIDX_TRG write 11902-11903); iwx_rx_pkt 11433-11874 handles REPLY_RX_PHY/MPDU (iwx_rx_mpdu_mq 5827-5986), BA_NOTIF (compressed BA 6063-6110), TX_CMD (6152-6203), MISSED_BEACONS (directed probe 6205-6248), ALIVE, STATISTICS, CT_KILL, PNVM/INIT complete, scan complete, MCC, ERROR, TIME_EVENT, session-protection, BAR_FRAME_RELEASE (bounds-checked 11807-11844), TLC_MNG_UPDATE_NOTIF (9574-9631) plus ~24 command-response copies; unhandled IDs log loudly (11846-11852). Replenishment inside the loop (11492).
findings.analysis: Ring never starves under load. Gaps noted: RX_NO_DATA_NOTIF ignored (11771-11772); no checksum validation in either direction (TX offload assist is only a payload-offset word, ItlTx.hpp:58-60). Reorder is a faithful OpenBSD port with timeout-driven release (4093-4155) and old-SN delba workaround (5576-5624). [report: with noted gaps]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a.

findings.title: Power management: always-on station PS; no WoW, no U-APSD, no SAR; sleep = full firmware reload
findings.evidence: PS unconditionally enabled: iwx_power_build_cmd 7389-7390 sets POWER_SAVE_ENA whenever not MONITOR; power_update_device 7421-7422 same. WoW: WOW TLV parsed into sections (1585-1590) but only REGULAR ever loaded (4899); no D3/wowlan command. U-APSD: TLV constants only (if_iwxreg.h:1210-1245). SAR/BIOS: zero matches for SAR/PPAG/GEO - TX power unmanaged. LTR: CSR write 1052-1078 + fw cmd gated sc_ltr_enabled (3021-3027, 5110-5122), skipped with SET_LTR_GEN2 (10669). Kext sleep: setPowerStateOff -> disableAdapter -> DVACT_QUIESCE -> iwx_stop (AirportItlwm.cpp:900-906; ItlIwx.cpp:274-285); wake restarts only if the stack re-enables (609-617, 13894-13919).
findings.analysis: Wake latency is a complete firmware reload (PNVM wait included, DRV-IWX-008) i.e. seconds, and correctness depends on macOS issuing enable() after wake - a fragile contract matching reported power-polish issues. No SAR enforcement is a regulatory-compliance exposure (LINUX-009).
findings.runtime_confirmation: macOS diagnostics kit: sleep/wake cycle then collect 08-kernel-log + 09-power (DRV-AP-006/007 guided check).

findings.title: Recovery/fault handling: interrupt-driven full reinit on any fatal event; aggressive state-machine error recovery
findings.evidence: SW_ERR/FH_ERR -> iwx_nic_error dump + task_add(init_task) (11976-12001, 12086-12111); HW_ERR -> flag + reinit (12003-12012, 12118-12125); CT_KILL -> HW_ERR + reinit (11619-11629); RF-KILL toggle -> reinit (11967-11974); TX watchdog 15 s (10914, 11021-11057). iwx_newstate_task 10248-10254: any error in auth/assoc/run -> full firmware restart. iwx_init retry loop 10779-10791 retries exactly once. No unbounded loops (iwx_poll_bit 2300-2319, prepare_card_hw 10x150 ms 2984-2996); iwx_nic_lock underflow panic remains live (2347-2352).
findings.analysis: No in-place recovery and no error is ever contained: a single failed session-protection or quota command during association restarts the radio, visible to macOS as a link flap. Combined with DRV-IWX-009's short command timeout this plausibly produces the join-unreliability symptom. [report: design amplifies transients]
findings.runtime_confirmation: macOS diagnostics kit: 08-kernel-log during join attempts - error dumps + reinit sequences (SW_ERR/HW_ERR dumps are always-enabled logs, 11113/11977/12089).

findings.title: Concurrency model: one workloop gate; splnet() is a no-op; all KASSERTs compile away
findings.evidence: timeout.c:32-39: int splnet() { return 1; } / void splx(int s) {} - ~25 HAL spl sites get zero mutual exclusion. Real serialization: every entry re-dispatches via getMainCommandGate()->runAction when !inGate() (6513-6519, 3270-3278, 13351-13357, all five task bodies); timers via CTimeout on the command gate (timeout.c:41-70); interrupt on same workloop. Proof KASSERT is non-evaluating: iwx_stop 10966 references task_refs whose struct field is commented out (if_iwxvar.h:603) yet the file compiles - all ~25 KASSERTs discarded. iwx_nic_lock (CSR handshake) held across iwx_tvqm_alloc_txq's synchronous command sleep in ba_task (4611-4630).
findings.analysis: The single-gate model is internally consistent (all traced paths funnel through the gate - no provable race found); but dead assertions mean the original OpenBSD invariant checks no longer guard anything, and any future ungated path silently becomes a race. [report: CONFIRMED DEFECT for dead assertions; VALIDATED for the locking model]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a - structural; kernel instrumentation only.

findings.title: iwx_start uses attemptAction (non-WCL builds): start attempts silently dropped when the gate is busy
findings.evidence: iwx_start 10922-10932: #ifdef AIRPORT_WCL uses runAction; #else uses attemptAction - which returns immediately with failure if the gate is held (e.g. by a sleeping sync command or newstate_task).
findings.analysis: When the output thread's start attempt is dropped, transmission resumes only when something else re-kicks the queue; iwx_clear_oactive calls signalOutputThread (6057-6059, __PRIVATE_SPI__) on completions which likely papers over it, but a dropped start after the last completion can leave frames parked in if_snd. Candidate contributor to intermittent throughput stalls; the WCL build already switched to blocking runAction (telling).
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a on the WCL Sequoia target (non-WCL path compiled out); monitor legacy builds only.

findings.title: ~21 MB static footprint of the HAL softc (512 TX rings x 1024 slots)
findings.evidence: if_iwxvar.h:630: struct iwx_tx_ring txq[IWX_MAX_TVQM_QUEUES]; with 512 queues (if_iwxreg.h:1756), each ring embedding data[1024] ~40 B (if_iwxvar.h:353; gen3 1024-slot size if_iwxreg.h:1823); plus sc_cmd_resp_pkt/sc_cmd_resp_len 65536x2 (~1 MB, :723-724) and sc_iml[20480] (:686). Arithmetic ~21.5 MB wired kernel memory per instance before any runtime allocation.
findings.analysis: The AX211 target can create at most ~11 queues (8 agg TIDs + cmd + aux + mgmt) - 100x oversized for the stated AX211-only mission and inflates every ItlIwx allocation. Tier-2 should size txq[] to the firmware's actual TVQM limit (16-32) or make ring data arrays pointers. [report: resource bloat]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a - visible as wired kernel memory per instance; kextalloc/vm stats via macOS kit 09.

findings.title: IWX_DEBUG hard-enabled and iwx_debug=1: every firmware command logged in all builds
findings.evidence: 134-139: #define IWX_DEBUG ... int iwx_debug = 1; DPRINTF(x) { if (iwx_debug > 0) XYLog x; }. Level>=1 sites include the per-command send log (6687) and rate-control log at every TX fill (6913); error dumps wrapped in #if 1 'always enabled for now' (11113, 11977, 12089).
findings.analysis: iwx_tx_fill_cmd's log runs on the TX path of every non-aggregated frame and iwx_send_cmd's for every command - measurable workloop-time cost and unified-log flood in exactly the paths that need to be fast for scan/join polish. Not build-gated: Release would ship the same logging (cross-ref REPO-004).
findings.runtime_confirmation: macOS diagnostics kit: 08-kernel-log - the spam rate is directly observable in the unified log.

findings.title: Off-by-one bounds checks in rate pretty-printers (OOB read)
findings.evidence: iwx_rs_pretty_ant 518-531: 4-entry table, guard if (ant > ARRAY_SIZE(ant_name)) lets ant==4 (ANT_C, if_iwxreg.h:5777) pass and read ant_name[4]. Same in iwx_rs_pretty_bw 533-547 (bw==5 passes). Both invoked from iwx_rs_update 9593-9598 on every TLC rate notification, not debug-gated.
findings.analysis: 1-byte-past-end read of a const char*[] in a hot logging path; cosmetic crash risk only; fix is >=. Unlikely on the 2-antenna AX211 target, reachable on 3-antenna radios.
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a - source-confirmed; bounded by TLC antenna-field width (open question 6).

findings.title: Dead code / OpenBSD-isms inventory (quality)
findings.evidence: Verified present: #if 0 fw-debug destination block with author uncertainty (1126-1136); #ifdef notyet x3 (6/7 GHz list 416-422, 1024-slot gen3 TVQM, beacon filter 9917-9929); commented-out onLoadFW/OSKextRequestResource remnant (1406-1419); unreachable statement (7614-7616); dead guard on uint8_t tid (4699); bus_dmamap_sync commented out at 12+ sites with one live sync at 6171; iwx_ioctl generation re-entry guard now err==0 && false (11063-11074).
findings.analysis: None individually harmful; collectively they mark every place the port diverged from upstream without cleanup and hide real behavior changes (e.g. the ioctl re-entry guard is gone).

findings.title: iwx_intr legacy-MSI quirks and ICT fun
findings.evidence: iwx_intr 11906-12057: ICT walk with historical bit-shuffling (11937-11943 'don't ask'/'i am not expected to understand this'), all-ones bus-dead detection (11946), ALIVE -> reprogram all 512 RX descriptors + WIDX_TRG=8 (11956-11963), periodic-interrupt one-shot dance (12029-12046).

findings.title: Station/STA removal flows leave shared state consistent; run_stop iterates rxba correctly
findings.evidence: iwx_rm_sta 7646-7679: flush -> REMOVE_STA -> reset BA masks, delba per agreed TID; iwx_run_stop 9972-10044 tears down RX BA sessions synchronously ('We cannot rely on the BA task... separate thread') and drains+flushes (iwx_flush_sta 7262-7291: drain on, TXPATH_FLUSH all-TIDs, drain off); generation counters (sc_generation) guard every async-vs-reset race traced (4329, 4626, 10781, 13839).
findings.analysis: Teardown ordering is careful and matches OpenBSD's hard-won fixes. The only leak in the flow is DRV-IWX-011 (queue release).
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a.

findings.title: Native integration is WCL-message-native; legacy ioctl path intentionally severed
findings.evidence: AirportItlwmV2.cpp:1171-1180: apple80211_ioctl returns kIOReturnUnsupported under AIRPORT_WCL; apple80211SkywalkRequest x2 always Unsupported (1182-1194). Upward events via postMessage (WCL.cpp:343) using IO80211ControllerV2::postMessage (include/Airport/macOS15/IO80211ControllerV2.h:131).
findings.analysis: On Sequoia the driver speaks the real WCL PostOffice protocol (scan results as async beacon messages, join as candidate lists, driver availability lifecycle) - a fundamentally more native contract than legacy itlwm ioctl emulation. All remaining ioctl findings concern dead code on this target unless stated. [severity defaulted: report gives none]

findings.title: Probe/start lifecycle and interface publication are sound; hard OS version gate
findings.evidence: Two-stage match: IOPCIEDeviceWrapper::probe (IOPCIEDeviceWrapper.cpp:58-91) - single iwx_match branch (ItlIwm/ItlIwn removed by reduction), MSI-X disabled/MSI enabled, pciNub/fHalService stored for reuse; AirportItlwm::probe (V2.cpp:148-163) adopts them. start() 266-469: version gate if (version_major != 24 || version_minor < 2) return false; CC pipes before super::start; HAL attach; Skywalk interface + initWCL (374-384); attachInterface + deferBSDAttach(true) (402-419); RegistrationInfo + registerService (420-467). stop()/releaseAll()/free() ordering verified (471-510, 25-84).
findings.analysis: Ordering correct (HAL attach before interface creation; BSD attach deferred and gated). The version gate means the kext refuses to start on anything except macOS 15.2-15.x - correct for this machine (15.8.2, minor=8), protects against accidental Tahoe loads, makes the binary non-portable (see DRV-AP-015). [severity defaulted]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a.

findings.title: 6 GHz (Wi-Fi 6E) band entirely excluded from the native scan/channel path
findings.evidence: WCL.hpp:464-468 decodeScan: if (!channel || channel > 196 || (flags & 0x2000)) continue; - 6 GHz entries dropped ('Do not confuse 6 GHz channel numbers with overlapping 2.4 GHz ones'); set6G_MODE stub Unsupported (SkywalkInterface.hpp:357); getWCL_FW_HOT_CHANNELS/getCOUNTRY_BAND_SUPPORT stubbed (231-232); channel publication only distinguishes 2/5 GHz (WCL.cpp:935, 323); getSUPPORTED_CHANNELS maps only 2/5 flags (SkywalkInterface.cpp:836-851).
findings.analysis: AX211 hardware is 6E-capable but the WCL integration never advertises or scans 6 GHz; macOS will not show any 6 GHz networks. Deliberate scope cut, not a bug - caps the native experience for 6E APs (cross-ref DRV-11D-001, LINUX-004, REF-005).
findings.runtime_confirmation: Diagnostic kit DRV-11D-001 check: Ubuntu 04-wifi-caps (5955-7115 MHz) vs macOS 06-wifi-state near an active 6 GHz AP.

findings.title: WPA3-SAE-only and PMF-required networks unsupported; only PSK/SAE transition mode works (RSN IE rewrite)
findings.evidence: classifyLegacyAuth (WCL.hpp:506-529) accepts only WPA/WPA2/PSK/SHA256-PSK/8021X/SHA256-8021X; anything else (SAE bit, FT bits) -> Invalid -> startWCLJoin returns kIOReturnUnsupported (WCL.cpp:442-444). PMF never advertised (V2.cpp:981-995 zeroes MFP bit; legacy commented-out MFP-capable at 1000-1005). Transition networks handled by selectWPA2TransitionMode (WCL.hpp:343-425) rewriting the scan-message-copy RSN IE to WPA2-PSK, preserving PMF-capable 0x80 caps, stripping IE 244; validRSNOverride gates the WCL RSN write path; accessWCLRSN(write) Unsupported (WCL.cpp:396-401).
findings.analysis: Upstream WPA3-transition fix (7204c69, merged in baseline) properly integrated: mixed-mode networks connect using the in-driver PSK supplicant. Pure-SAE (WPA3-only) and PMF-required networks fail to join with unsupported status - macOS may show them (from scan IEs) but joins will not succeed. [report: UNSUPPORTED (SAE-only) + VALIDATED (transition)]

findings.title: Scan execution lives entirely in firmware; the net80211 scan state machine is dead code, and ic_state=S_SCAN is assigned directly by the HAL
findings.evidence: iwx_newstate_task case S_SCAN calls iwx_scan(sc) and returns without invoking sc->sc_newstate (ItlIwx.cpp:10221-10228); iwx_scan sets ic->ic_state = IEEE80211_S_SCAN (ItlIwx.cpp:9005) and for non-bgscans forces link DOWN + ieee80211_node_cleanup (9001-9004). net80211 S_SCAN case (proto.c:1529-1584, incl. begin_scan and per-channel PROBE_REQ generation) is reachable only from iwx_init (ItlIwx.cpp:10812). Firmware dwell config 7928-7931 (active=10, passive=110, fragmented=44, extended=90 TU); channel list = full ic_channels[] walk (7689-7729). SIOCS80211SCAN disabled (ieee80211_ioctl.c:865-867).
findings.analysis: Explains why dwell/channel-iteration logic cannot be tuned from the 802.11 layer and why scan behavior differs from native drivers. Also means ic_state==S_SCAN is true during firmware scans, which the beacon parser relies on (input.c:2075, 2158). No user-visible defect by itself; frames the rest of the scan findings. [report severity: Informational]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a - architecture fact.

findings.title: Autonomous roaming is fully disabled on macOS - IEEE80211_F_DESBSSID is latched for the whole association, blocking both the bgscan trigger and candidate selection (corrects prior audit DRV-AP-005's premise)
findings.evidence: Both macOS join paths pin the BSSID: WCL startWCLJoin does memcpy(ic_des_bssid, join.bssid, 6); ic_flags |= F_DESBSSID (WCL.cpp:513-515); legacy associateSSID same (SkywalkInterface.cpp:119-122). Flag cleared only in leaveWCLNetwork (WCL.cpp:611) and SIOCS80211BSSID (ioctl.c:726) - never during RUN. Two independent blocks: (1) RX-path bgscan armer refuses to arm while pinned (input.c:441-450 requires (ic_flags & F_DESBSSID) == 0); (2) ieee80211_match_bss rejects every other BSSID (node.c:1097-1099). The only scans while associated are WCL-requested, going through begin_cache_bgscan which sets F_DISABLE_BG_AUTO_CONNECT (ieee80211.c:143), making roamscan false in end_scan (node.c:1407-1408).
findings.analysis: The net80211 roam engine (bgscan_timeout -> begin_bgscan -> roam selection -> node_switch_bss) is unreachable in the Sequoia WCL build. Prior audit DRV-AP-005 assumed 'roaming is alive and well inside net80211' - it is not; the stale-joinBSSID symptoms it predicts actually arise from this pin plus the re-auth paths (DRV-11C-007). User-visible: no seamless BSS transitions; the driver stays on a deteriorating AP until it fully drops (beacon-miss -> full rescan), then - still pinned to the dead BSSID (DRV-11C-003) - cannot fail over to another BSSID of the same ESS. Primary code-level explanation for 'network switching feels wrong'.
findings.runtime_confirmation: Diagnostic kit DRV-11C-002 check: walk between two same-SSID APs while associated; 08-kernel-log shows no roam/transition events while signal degrades; Ubuntu 05/07 as known-good baseline.

findings.title: With no pending join, the driver scans forever - no idle park, no failover, 30 s dead-BSSID lockout
findings.evidence: ieee80211_end_scan 'notfound' path: node.c:1456-1484 - when no candidate matches, reset_scan + next_mode + next_scan restart the firmware scan, with comment 'This will loop forever until an access point is found' (1472-1475). On macOS nothing breaks the loop: match_bss returns ASSOCFAIL_ESSID for every node when !ic_wcl_join_requested (node.c:1058-1061), and WCL clears that flag only in finishWCLJoin(failure)/leaveWCLNetwork/stopWCL (WCL.cpp:574, 599, 105). After beacon-miss the same loop is entered with the DRV-11C-002 pin still active, so recovery waits for the 30 s WCL join timer (WCL.cpp:527, 581-588) or macOS re-issuing the join.
findings.analysis: Explains (a) 'Wi-Fi menu network list keeps changing/refreshing even when idle' (every end_scan also fires EVT_SCAN_DONE, node.c:1410-1411, and beacons continuously push EVT_BEACON), (b) elevated idle power/heat vs native (continuous off-channel scanning), and (c) the multi-second dead zone when walking away from an AP: beacon loss (~3 s, set_beacon_miss_threshold caps 30xTU, proto.c:1363-1382) + 5 s probe wait + pinned rescans. [severity normalized from Medium-High]
findings.runtime_confirmation: Diagnostic kit DRV-11C-003 check: leave Wi-Fi enabled but not connected for 5 minutes, then collect; 08-kernel-log shows repeating scan-start/done cycles with no user trigger.

findings.title: The 1 s watchdog runs on a dedicated workloop outside the command gate - it mutates MLME state concurrently with the RX thread and all other timers
findings.evidence: fWatchdogWorkLoop = IOWorkLoop::workLoop(); watchdogTimer = IOTimerEventSource::timerEventSource(...watchdogAction); added to the separate workloop (V2.cpp:345-361); watchdogAction calls if_watchdog and rearms every 1000 ms (V2.cpp:116-122; V2.hpp:37). iwx_watchdog -> ieee80211_watchdog (ItlIwx.cpp:11056) decrements ic_mgt_timer and on zero calls ieee80211_new_state(ic, S_SCAN, -1) (ieee80211.c:906-929) - a full state transition (stop AMPDU, free_allnodes, mgmt queue purge) executed on the watchdog thread with no lock. Meanwhile the RX thread on the main workloop sets ic_mgt_timer=0 on every beacon (input.c:2056-2057) and issues its own transitions. splnet() provides nothing (timeout.c:32-39). All other net80211 timers go through CTimeout on the main workloop (timeout.c:46-49) - this one is the outlier.
findings.analysis: A decrement/zero race is narrow but real: auth response lands (RX thread, sets S_ASSOC) in the window where the watchdog has just read ic_mgt_timer==1 - the watchdog then calls new_state(SCAN), queueing a SCAN task that can land after the RUN task, tearing down a just-established association (or the dedup at ItlIwx.cpp:10273 silently eats one transition, leaving ic_state and hardware out of sync). Plausible contributor to rare 'join succeeded then immediately dropped' and 'stuck in SCAN' reports; also fires during system wake while firmware is still stopped. The structural violation (ungated state mutation) is unambiguous. [report: structure High/High, manifestation Medium/Medium]
findings.runtime_confirmation: Kit 08-kernel-log across wake: watchdog SCAN transitions vs iwx_newstate_task completions (open question 1).

findings.title: Association rejection is never retried directly and never poisons the AP - 5 s stall -> full rescan -> same AP re-selected -> loop until the 30 s WCL timer
findings.evidence: ieee80211_recv_assoc_resp failure path only does if (ni != ic->ic_bss) ni->ni_fails++; then returns (input.c:2745-2755) - for the normal case ni==ic_bss so no failure is recorded and no retry is scheduled; state stays S_ASSOC with ic_mgt_timer still counting down from the ASSOC_REQ (set in send_mgmt, output.c:2024, TRANS_WAIT=5, node.h:54). The watchdog then does new_state(ic, S_SCAN, -1) (ieee80211.c:928) - a complete rescan. choose_bss skips nodes only when ni_fails set (node.c:1336-1345), so the freshly-rejected AP (no fails) is selected again. Contrast the AUTH path which retries up to 3 times in place (ieee80211.c:921-924).
findings.analysis: Against an AP that answers auth but rejects association (band-steering, client limit, 802.11r-only SSID, transient TRY_AGAIN_LATER), the join degenerates into scan->auth->reject->5 s->rescan cycles until WCL's 30 s joinTimer fails the join (WCL.cpp:527, 581-588). User-visible as 'joining spins for ~30 s then fails'; also floods the RF environment with rescans. Correct behavior would be an immediate in-place assoc retry (2-3 attempts) before rescanning, and recording ni_fails on the bss node. [severity normalized from Medium-High; report confidence High (code path), Medium (frequency)]
findings.runtime_confirmation: Reproduce against an AP that rejects association (hostapd max_num_sta=0 or deny-MAC) - open question 4.

findings.title: Auth-timeout ni_fails poisoning removes failed APs from subsequent scan results
findings.evidence: Watchdog auth timeout: ni = find_node(ic_bss->ni_macaddr); if (ni) ni->ni_fails++; (ieee80211.c:917-919). choose_bss: if (ni->ni_fails) { if (ni->ni_fails++ > 2) ieee80211_free_node(ic, ni); continue; } (node.c:1336-1345). ni_fails cleared only on reaching RUN (proto.c:1725-1728) or node re-creation.
findings.analysis: After 1-3 auth timeouts (AP briefly overloaded, or the DRV-11C-005 rescan loop timing out at AUTH), the AP's node is skipped in selection and - worse - freed from the node table on the next scan round; nodes are what WCL beacon-push uses (EVT_BEACON per frame), so the network can vanish from the Wi-Fi menu for one or more scan cycles after a failed join attempt. 'Network disappears from list after failed attempt, comes back later' symptom class.
findings.runtime_confirmation: Kit 08-kernel-log collected right after failed join attempts; observe menu behavior across subsequent scans.

findings.title: AP-initiated deauth triggers silent auto-reauth while WCL/airportd are told the link died - and never told it came back
findings.evidence: ieee80211_recv_deauth (STA): if (!(roamscan || stay_auth)) new_state(ic, S_AUTH, DEAUTH) (input.c:2951-2962); newstate S_AUTH-from-RUN with mgt=DEAUTH sends AUTH seq 1 immediately - 'try to reauth' (proto.c:1618-1634). Upward only EVT_STA_DEAUTH is emitted (input.c:2946-2948). WCL's handler sets portAuthorized=false, forces LQM invalid, posts Deauth; because joinPending is false while associated, finishWCLJoin no-ops (WCL.cpp:788-797, 556-559). The subsequent successful re-auth/re-assoc runs entirely below WCL: EVT_STA_ASSOC_DONE is ignored when !joinPending (WCL.cpp:776-786), and handleWCLLink(up) only posts LinkStatus-up inside the first-beacon join-completion path (WCL.cpp:624-640, 747-763). set_link_state additionally asserts LINK_STATE_DOWN at the top of every state transition (proto.c:1445), so setLinkStatus stops the output thread and flushes queues on each reauth (V2.cpp:654-662).
findings.analysis: For a transient deauth (AP reboot, band-steer, 802.11r BSS transition) the chip re-associates within ~1-2 s, but airportd saw Deauth + Link-down and never a Link-up; it will typically drop the DHCP lease, show 'connection lost', or trigger its own rejoin that then fights the driver's in-flight reauth (scan/join Busy, cross-ref AP-008). Same-BSSID twin of the roam staleness in AP-005 and a direct 'status staleness / spurious disconnect' mechanism. [confidence normalized from Medium-High]
findings.runtime_confirmation: Kit open question 2: log WCL setWCL_ASSOCIATE timing vs EVT_STA_DEAUTH; watch whether airportd re-issues a join (join-storm vs silent reconnect).

findings.title: Upward notification inventory is minimal - no disassoc, roam, beacon-miss, or port-authorized events exist
findings.evidence: The complete event set is STA_ASSOC_DONE/STA_DEAUTH/COUNTRY_CODE_UPDATE/SCAN_DONE/BEACON/DRIVER_READY/DRIVER_STOPPED/DRIVER_RESET_BEGIN (ieee80211_var.h:687-695). Emitters: end_scan (SCAN_DONE, node.c:1410), recv_probe_resp (BEACON, input.c:2179-2189), recv_assoc_resp (ASSOC_DONE incl. failures in WCL build, input.c:2735-2743), recv_deauth (DEAUTH, input.c:2946), HAL (DRIVER_*). ieee80211_recv_disassoc emits nothing (input.c:3012-3023). Beacon-miss (iwx_rx_bmiss -> directed probe, ItlIwx.cpp:6205-6248) emits nothing. 4-way completion (ni_port_valid=1, pae_input.c:688-693) emits nothing - join success is instead inferred from the first beacon (WCL.cpp:747-763), adding ~100 ms and a failure mode: join 'succeeds' only if a beacon is heard.
findings.analysis: macOS learns about link life almost exclusively by polling and the IOKit link-status side channel; every recovery the driver performs on its own (reauth, rekey, rescan) is invisible. Report enumerates an 11-row notification-gap table with the WCL consumer for each. [report: CONFIRMED contract gap]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a - structural; see the 11-row gap table in source report.

findings.title: The in-driver supplicant has no STA-side handshake timeout; wrong-PSK and stalled handshakes are bounded only by WCL's 30 s timer or the AP's patience
findings.evidence: After successful association with RSN, recv_assoc_resp sets ni_rsn_supp_state = RSNA_SUPP_PTKSTART and - with the OpenBSD ic_mgt_timer=5 line commented out - leaves no timeout (input.c:2911-2913); S_RUN entry clears ic_mgt_timer (proto.c:1729). The EAPOL retry machinery (ni_eapol_to, ni_rsn_retries > 3 deauth) exists only on the AP side: timeout_set(&ni->ni_eapol_to, ...) and all senders of msg1/msg3 are #ifndef IEEE80211_STA_ONLY (node.c:1750-1753; pae_output.c:139, 276-290, 389+). If msg1/4 never arrives, nothing in net80211 recovers; WCL's joinTimer (30 s, WCL.cpp:527) is the sole backstop. Wrong-PSK flow: msg3 MIC check fails -> silent return (pae_input.c:425-429) -> AP retransmits msg3 -> eventually AP deauths reason 15/16 -> DRV-11C-007 path. If msg4 is lost after a successful msg3, the replay counter is already advanced (544-545) and retransmitted msg3s are discarded as replays (401-406) - recovery depends entirely on the AP deauthing.
findings.analysis: 'Wrong password' and 'AP ignores handshake' cases take up to 30 s to surface as a join failure, and present to macOS as a deauth/disconnect rather than an auth failure with a reason code. Contributes to join-unreliability perception. [report: CONFIRMED (gap) + UNVERIFIED (recovery stall); severity normalized from Medium-High; stall confidence Low-Medium]
findings.runtime_confirmation: Kit DRV-11D-003 check (wrong-PSK join); controlled AP dropping msg4 once (open question 5).

findings.title: PTK/GTK installation into the firmware is asynchronous and unacknowledged - first encrypted downstream traffic can race the key install
findings.evidence: iwx_set_key sends IWX_ADD_STA_KEY with IWX_CMD_ASYNC and returns immediately (ItlIwx.cpp:10053-10084). In msg3 processing, msg4 is sent before the key install (pae_input.c:552-554 then 580-596); the EBUSY -> deferlink path (590-592, 632-634) exists but iwx never returns EBUSY; there is no completion callback that would re-check deferlink.
findings.analysis: EAPOL msg4 itself is unencrypted so the classic race is harmless; the residual risk is the AP's first encrypted data/GTK-dependent multicast arriving before the firmware has the key (dropped frames immediately after join - 'first ping/ARP after connect lost' reports). Small window; flag for runtime verification rather than as a confirmed defect. [severity normalized from Low-Medium]
findings.runtime_confirmation: Kit: first-ping/ARP timing immediately after join (open question 6).

findings.title: Scan-result cache lifecycle is split-brained: roam-bgscans wipe the node table, WCL cache-bgscans retain it for 5 minutes, and STA-mode aging timers are never armed
findings.evidence: ieee80211_begin_bgscan calls free_allnodes(ic, 0 /* keep ic_bss */) before every roam-capable bgscan (ieee80211.c:111-119). begin_cache_bgscan (the only one WCL triggers, WCL.cpp:270-271) keeps nodes unless the last cache scan was >5 min ago (ieee80211.c:145-150). The STA-mode inactivity timers are not installed: timeout_set(ic_inact_timeout/...cache_timeout) is inside if (ic_caps & (HOSTAP | IBSS)) (node.c:741-755) - iwx sets neither cap - so ni_inact advances only via node_raise_inact at begin_scan (node.c:843-847, 879-882) and clean_inactive_nodes(INACT_SCAN=10) at each end_scan (node.c:1422-1423, 2341-2362). ni_age_ts is only maintained under #ifdef AIRPORT (input.c:1956-1958), which the WCL build does not define.
findings.analysis: There is no coherent 'result age' the upper layer can rely on: mid-roam-bgscan the table is empty except ic_bss (any snapshot walk sees almost nothing), while WCL cache-scans serve nodes up to 5 minutes old with no age field (cross-ref AP-010). Nodes seen only in beacons during a scan can persist across multiple menu-open refreshes. Explains stale/missing entries in the Wi-Fi menu and the 'AP I turned off still shows' report class.
findings.runtime_confirmation: Kit DRV-AP-011 comparison: macOS vs Ubuntu network lists at the same spot.

findings.title: RSSI handling is last-frame-wins on 2.4 GHz and max-hold on 5 GHz - no smoothing; band choice at selection time prefers 5 GHz above fixed thresholds
findings.evidence: recv_probe_resp: on 5 GHz during scan, probe-response RSSI is preferred and beacons can only raise the stored value (input.c:2158-2169); on 2.4 GHz (and all bands outside scan) ni->ni_rssi = rxi->rxi_rssi - every beacon overwrites (2170-2171). Selection prefers the best-5 GHz AP when it passes checkrssi (thresholds -70 dBm/40% for 5 GHz, -60 dBm/50% for 2.4 GHz; node.c:1378-1391, 1722-1742; var.h:220-223). ESS scoring adds +32 known SSID, +21 zero past failures, +16/+8 RSN/WPA, 5 GHz bonus (node.c:466-506).
findings.analysis: 2.4 GHz RSSI jumps frame-to-frame, so the menu's ordering of 2.4 GHz networks can shuffle between scans, and the WCL-published rssi (WCL.cpp:328) inherits the jitter. Not a defect per se (upstream behavior) but a plausible source of 'signal bars keep changing' reports; native drivers average. [severity normalized from Low-Medium; report confidence High (code), Low (impact)]
findings.runtime_confirmation: Kit: repeated 06-wifi-state samples; observe bar ordering between scans.

findings.title: Hidden-SSID handling works only via directed probes, and an SSID whose first byte is NUL can never be learned
findings.evidence: Node SSID is learned only from a non-empty SSID IE when the stored one is empty: if (ssid[1] != 0 && ni->ni_essid[0] == 0) (input.c:2151-2156) - the probe-response override for hidden networks (comment 2144-2150). Directed probes are firmware-generated from ic_wcl_scan_ssid (WCL scans, ItlIwx.cpp:8068-8074, 8206-8219) or ic_des_essid (join-triggered, 8065-8067); broadcast scans set PASSIVE when scanActive false (8220-8221). A network whose real SSID begins with 0x00 keeps ni_essid[0]=='\0' forever, so a second beacon/probe can never update it and join matching (memcmp against ic_des_essid, node.c:1093-1096) compares against a truncated name.
findings.analysis: Hidden networks are joinable (verified logic) but absent from broadcast scans (by design) - if macOS asks for a broadcast scan only, hidden APs do not appear until airportd issues the directed scan. The NUL-first-byte quirk is an edge case mostly affecting exotic SSIDs. [report: VALIDATED (directed path) + CONFIRMED minor DEFECT (NUL-first-byte)]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a.

findings.title: 6 GHz (Wi-Fi 6E) is excluded at the NVM channel table; net80211 has no 6 GHz band support at all
findings.evidence: The ultra-high-band channel list is compiled out: iwx_nvm_channels_uhb[] = {...14x2.4, 40x5, #ifdef notyet ...6-7 GHz... #endif} (ItlIwx.cpp:409-423); sc_uhb_supported selects that (identical) list (3908-3914). In net80211, mhz2ieee/ieee2mhz only understand 2.4/5 GHz mappings (ieee80211.c:299-362), no IEEE80211_CHAN_6GHZ-style flag exists anywhere, and iwx_umac_scan_fill_channels maps everything non-2.4 to PHY_BAND_5 (ItlIwx.cpp:7708-7711). ieee80211_he_supported additionally refuses any AP whose HE Operation advertises 6GHZ_OP_INFO (proto.c:931-933).
findings.analysis: AX211 hardware + API-68 firmware can do 6 GHz; the port cannot even represent it. 6E APs are invisible in scans. Enabling requires the notyet channel list, band plumbing in net80211 (freq<->chan maps, flags, probe/EDCA handling) and scan band fields - a substantial feature port, not a bugfix. Confirms AP-003 at the 802.11 layer (cross-ref LINUX-004, REF-005).
findings.runtime_confirmation: Kit DRV-11D-001 check: Ubuntu 04-wifi-caps (5955-7115 MHz) vs macOS 06-wifi-state near an active 6 GHz AP.

findings.title: Regulatory control is passive-by-NVM only - no regdomain enforcement layer; DFS/passive channels never probed (WCL path); country changes never reshape the channel list
findings.evidence: ieee80211_regdomain.c contains only name<->country-code<->domain lookup tables (59-197); nothing applies a domain mask to ic_chan_active. Channel flags come straight from NVM (IWX_NVM_CHANNEL_VALID/ACTIVE/DFS, ItlIwx.cpp:3916-3985) with CHAN_PASSIVE/CHAN_DFS set (3951-3983). Probe gating: AirportWCL::probeChannel(active, passiveOnly, dfs) = active && !passiveOnly && !dfs (WCL.hpp:426-428) applied per channel (ItlIwx.cpp:7720-7726); the non-WCL fallback would probe passive channels on directed scans (7724). Country IE/EVT_COUNTRY_CODE_UPDATE flows to WCL (WCL.cpp:656-657) but does not modify scanning; world-roaming defaults equal the NVM SKU profile.
findings.analysis: Regulatorily conservative (good), but macOS's country-code setting is cosmetic for this driver; users in domains with more 5 GHz spectrum see no benefit, and passive-channel-only discovery (110 TU dwell beacons) makes sparse-DFS environments feel slow to populate the menu. [report: VALIDATED (safety) / UNSUPPORTED (policy); severity Low (safety), capability dimension Medium]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a.

findings.title: Timer framework is sound on the main workloop, but stop/free ordering has latent hazards and the watchdog is the odd one out
findings.evidence: timeout_add/del/pending marshal through _fCommandGate->runAction (timeout.c:41-75); callbacks (CTimeout::timeoutOccurred, CTimeout.cpp:25-39) run as workloop event sources, serialized with the gate and RX; timeout_free removes and releases the event source (CTimeout.cpp:79-95). Teardown: ifdetach deletes/frees ic_bgscan_timeout (ieee80211.c:276-277); node timers freed in ba_free/node_cleanup (node.c:2059-2078, 1661-1686). Hazards: (a) node_detach frees ic_bss before free_allnodes (node.c:795-800) - a firing timer on another node during free_allnodes is prevented only by workloop serialization; (b) iwx_stop clears state on the gate while the watchdog workloop can be mid-watchdog (DRV-11C-004); (c) on sleep disableAdapter stops the firmware but the watchdog keeps ticking and can fire new_state(SCAN) against a dead radio (bounded by the SHUTDOWN check ItlIwx.cpp:10170-10175, but ieee80211_watchdog's read-modify of ic_mgt_timer is unprotected).
findings.analysis: The CTimeout design is actually the port's strongest piece; the risk is concentrated in the watchdog (11C-004) and sleep/wake transitions. Symptom class: 'weird state right after wake' reports. [report: VALIDATED (CTimeout) + UNVERIFIED (ordering); severity normalized from Low-Medium]
findings.runtime_confirmation: Kit: sleep/wake with 08-kernel-log covering the wake window.

findings.title: Every MLME transition forces LINK_STATE_DOWN at entry - link flaps during auth->assoc->run and on every reauth
findings.evidence: ieee80211_newstate line 1 of substance: set_link_state(ic, LINK_STATE_DOWN) (proto.c:1445). set_link_state maps DOWN to controller->setLinkStatus(kIONetworkLinkValid) (proto.c:1766-1774), which in V2 stops the BSD output thread and flushes both the data and mgmt queues (V2.cpp:654-662). UP is restored only at RUN entry (non-RSN) or at 4-way completion (RSN; pae_input.c:688-693, gated AIRPORT_WCL early-return in set_link_state proto.c:1745-1750).
findings.analysis: During a join each state hop bounces en0's link; during the auto-reauth of DRV-11C-007 the interface drops and rises while airportd was never told why. macOS tolerates it, but link-flap events are exactly what airportd uses to invalidate its association state - feeding the 'status staleness' symptom. [report: design with user-visible side effect; severity normalized from Low-Medium]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a - visible in ifconfig link state during joins.

findings.title: iwx_newstate silently drops duplicate transitions - pending-state overwrite can lose a transition and desync ic_state from hardware
findings.evidence: if (sc->ns_nstate == nstate && nstate != S_SCAN && nstate != S_AUTH) return 0; (ItlIwx.cpp:10273-10275). sc->ns_nstate/ns_arg are single slots written by iwx_newstate (10291-10292) and consumed by the task (10163-10166); a second transition request queued before the task runs overwrites both (no queueing).
findings.analysis: Fast sequences generated by the watchdog/RX race of DRV-11C-004 (e.g. SCAN requested while a RUN task is pending, or two different-arg AUTH requests) can collapse into one hardware action while net80211's ic_state advances twice (or vice versa). Candidate for the rare 'driver says associated, firmware never authed' wedge that only a radio toggle fixes. Needs runtime tracing to confirm frequency. [severity normalized from Low-Medium]
findings.runtime_confirmation: Runtime tracing of newstate_task completions vs requests (open question 1); kit 08-kernel-log across wake.

findings.title: Directed-scan abort semantics are handled WCL-side with a one-shot guard; net80211 has no abort notion at all
findings.evidence: The upstream 'directed-request abort completion' fix is present: scanSkipCompletion is set when a WCL scan starts while ic_state==S_SCAN with a directed SSID in flight (WCL.cpp:260-262) and consumes exactly one EVT_SCAN_DONE (766-775). The abort itself: iwx_scan aborts an in-flight bgscan before issuing the foreground scan (ItlIwx.cpp:8974-8981); the aborted scan's completion funnels through iwx_endscan -> ieee80211_end_scan (10300-10317) with net80211's F_BGSCAN still set, which the bgscan path clears (node.c:1494-1498). Both SCAN_COMPLETE_UMAC and SCAN_ITERATION_COMPLETE_UMAC feed iwx_endscan (ItlIwx.cpp:11698-11710).
findings.analysis: net80211's scan state is abort-agnostic (it only reacts to end_scan), so correctness rests entirely on the WCL guard's single-shot depth; a fragmented scan emitting an extra ITERATION_COMPLETE during the new scan still completes the WCL scan early (AP-009's residual). No new defect found at the 802.11 layer; documented to close the loop on the prior fix.
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a - cross-ref AP-009 for the residual race; kit 08-kernel-log.

findings.title: GTK/IGTK group rekey handling in STA mode is complete and correct, including re-marking the port and re-asserting link-up
findings.evidence: ieee80211_recv_rsn_group_msg1 (pae_input.c:833-994): replay check, MIC, KEK decrypt, GTK KDE parse, must_update_group_key anti-reinstall check (366-373), ic_set_key install, ni_port_valid=1 + set_link_state(UP) on SECURE, replay counter advance, msg2 sent. WPA1 variant at 999+ mirrors it. IGTK (MFP) handled at 934-966. 4-way msg3 carries GTK/IGTK KDEs with encrypted-key enforcement (pae_input.c:495-504, 604-677).
findings.analysis: Group rekey (the common 1 h-24 h AP rotation) will not drop the link; set_link_state(UP) re-runs are no-ops when already up (proto.c:1766). No user-visible defect expected from GTK handling. [severity defaulted]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a.

findings.title: Association status reporting is binary and lossy - auth failures produce no assoc event, failure reasons reach WCL only as a status word
findings.evidence: ic_assoc_status is set from the assoc resp status (input.c:2735) and ic_deauth_reason from deauth (2945); recv_auth resets both before dispatch (2345-2346). EVT_STA_ASSOC_DONE fires for assoc resp success and failure in the WCL build (#ifndef AIRPORT_WCL removed the success gate, input.c:2736-2743), but nothing is emitted for: auth rejection (ieee80211_auth_open status!=0 -> try_another_bss, proto.c:1341-1352, no event), auth/assoc timeout (watchdog path, no event), or the WCL join timeout itself. WCL's AssociationEvent carries only status (WCL.cpp:776-786).
findings.analysis: macOS error reporting for failed joins ('incorrect password', 'timeout', 'cannot connect') has almost nothing to work with; airportd must infer from Deauth reason codes after the fact. Contributes to unhelpful join-failure UX. [severity normalized from Low-Medium]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a.

findings.title: Beacon processing in RUN deliberately freezes RSN/HE parameters - correct against beacon loss, but security/HE changes require a rescan to be noticed
findings.evidence: RSN/WPA IE parsing runs only if (ic_state == S_SCAN || (ic_flags & F_BGSCAN)) (input.c:2075-2142); ieee80211_update_he_params refuses to erase a live association's HE context on beacon omission (if (ni != ic->ic_bss || ic_state != S_RUN) ni->ni_flags &= ~(HECAP|HEOP|...), 1656-1689); ERP/HT-protection/slot-time updates are applied live from beacons (1964-2058).
findings.analysis: Once associated, the driver cannot see an AP that changes its RSN IE (e.g. toggles WPA3-transition) until the next scan - acceptable and upstream-faithful; listed so future auditors do not flag it as a bug. [severity defaulted]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a.

findings.title: Auth retry policy is 3 in-place attempts with 5 s spacing, then full rescan - total worst-case latency budget ~20 s before the WCL 30 s timer
findings.evidence: ieee80211_send_mgmt arms ic_mgt_timer = TRANS_WAIT (5) for PROBE_REQ/AUTH/ASSOC_REQ (output.c:1989, 2003, 2024; node.h:54). Watchdog: auth timeout -> ni_fails++, retry join_bss while ni_fails < 3 (ieee80211.c:917-924); assoc timeout -> straight to SCAN (925-928). Beacon-miss -> directed probe (ItlIwx.cpp:6244) with its own 5 s timer; beacons reset the timer (input.c:2050-2057).
findings.analysis: A full join against a slow AP can legitimately take 3x(auth 5 s) + rescan time; combined with DRV-11C-005's non-retrying assoc this is the mechanical reason joins on this hardware feel much slower than native (~1-2 s). Latency budget, not corruption. [severity defaulted]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a.

findings.title: EVT_BEACON is emitted for every beacon/probe frame on every channel - WCL pushes each as a scan result while scanning, with no dedup window
findings.evidence: recv_probe_resp tail: ic_event_handler(ic, IEEE80211_EVT_BEACON, &event) with the raw IE blob (input.c:2179-2189); WCL publishes a BeaconMetadata message per event while scanPending || joinPending || state==SCAN || (portAuthorized && bssid==joinBSSID) (WCL.cpp:744-746, 307-345). With the DRV-11C-003 idle scan loop this is a continuous message stream even when the menu is closed.
findings.analysis: Correct-but-chatty: per-beacon allocation (IOMalloc per message, WCL.cpp:317-318) and PostOffice traffic scale with beacon rate x channels swept; on the idle scan loop this is a steady background cost (power/log volume - cross-ref DRV-IWX-021's unconditional debug logging amplifying the same paths).
findings.runtime_confirmation: Kit DRV-11C-003 check: measure EVT_BEACON/message rate while idle-disconnected (open question 3).

findings.title: ieee80211_free_allnodes' keep-current-BSS test compares BSSID and strncmp of SSIDs - a matching pair on another channel can be freed while a differing SSID on the same BSSID is kept
findings.evidence: node.c:2144-2149: if (!clear_ic_bss && ic->ic_bss != NULL) { if (memcmp(ic_bss->ni_bssid, ni->ni_bssid, 6) == 0 && strncmp(ic_bss->ni_essid, ni->ni_essid, NWID_LEN) == 0) continue; } - strncmp stops at the first NUL, so SSIDs equal up to the shorter one's NUL compare equal (e.g. 'Net' vs 'Net\0x41...'), and any node whose BSSID differs is freed even if it is the same network multi-BSSID set the driver might want cached.
findings.analysis: Edge-case cache churn during bgscan; no crash risk. Noted for completeness; fixing it would use a length-aware comparison (ni_esslen). [confidence normalized from Medium-High]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a.

findings.title: 6 GHz band excluded at the exact line of an #ifdef notyet
findings.evidence: ItlIwx.cpp:409-423: iwx_nvm_channels_uhb[] = { 2.4 GHz 1..14, 5 GHz 36..181, #ifdef notyet 6-7 GHz 1..233 #endif } - compiled table identical to the 2.4/5 GHz iwx_nvm_channels_8000 table. Device configs set .uhb_supported=1 (12246-12326) and iwx_init_channel_map selects the uhb table (3908-3914). ieee80211_ieee2mhz maps any channel >=27 to 5000+chan*5 (ieee80211.c:342-362); no IEEE80211_CHAN_6GHZ flag exists anywhere in itl80211/. WCL decodeScan drops entries carrying the 6 GHz flag (WCL.hpp: if (!channel || channel > 196 || (flags & 0x2000)) continue;).
findings.analysis: The AX211 radio is operated as a Wi-Fi 6 (not 6E) device; all 6 GHz BSSes are invisible. Because 6 GHz mandates WPA3-SAE, this exclusion also masks the SAE/GCMP gaps below (DRV-11D-002/003). Prior audit predicted this; exclusion confirmed.
findings.runtime_confirmation: Diagnostic kit DRV-11D-001 check: on Ubuntu confirm AX211 exposes 6 GHz (04-wifi-caps 5955-7115 MHz); on macOS stand near an active 6 GHz AP and scan (06-wifi-state).

findings.title: No GCMP cipher - WPA3 cipher suites unrepresentable
findings.evidence: Cipher set implemented = WEP40/104, TKIP, CCMP, BIP only: ieee80211_cipher_keylen (crypto.c:133-149), ieee80211_set_key (151-182); no ieee80211_crypto_gcmp.c in the tree; ieee80211_parse_rsn_cipher (input.c:1423-1457) accepts selectors {0,1,2,4,5,6} only - GCMP-128/256 (8/9) parse as CIPHER_NONE, causing parse_rsn_body to fail the AKM/IE checks.
findings.analysis: Any GCMP-only AP (typical WPA3-Enterprise, all 6 GHz) cannot be negotiated. On GCMP-capable WPA2/WPA3-mixed APs the stack silently falls back to CCMP if offered. Even Eric's fork lacks crypto_gcmp.c (REF-004) - WPA3-Enterprise remains blocked in all trees.
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a.

findings.title: WPA3-SAE cannot authenticate; the WPA3->WPA2 'fake' hack is compiled out of the WCL target
findings.evidence: ieee80211_recv_auth (input.c:2330-2344): 'only open auth mode is supported' - SAE (algorithm 3) frames are counted is_rx_auth_unsupported and dropped. The block mapping APPLE80211_AUTHTYPE_WPA3_SAE -> WPA2_PSK is inside #ifndef AIRPORT_WCL (SkywalkInterface.cpp:128-141) - not compiled for the Sequoia WCL build (pbxproj:1893-1901 defines only AIRPORT_WCL, AIRPORT_VTD, AIRPORT, IO80211FAMILY_V2).
findings.analysis: On a WPA3-SAE network the join request leaves the driver with no RSN protos/PSK (setASSOCIATION sets ic_psk only for WPA/WPA2/SHA256 PSK authtypes, SkywalkInterface.cpp:147-154); the stack attempts an open/no-encryption style flow that the AP rejects. WPA3-only SSIDs (and all 6 GHz) are unjoinable; WPA2/WPA3 transition-mode networks still work via WPA2. [report: capability defect]
findings.runtime_confirmation: Diagnostic kit DRV-11D-003 check: try to join a WPA3-SAE network on macOS, then collect 08-kernel-log; note what the Wi-Fi menu reported.

findings.title: MFP/PMF (802.11w) not advertised; IGTK path dead
findings.evidence: IWX capabilities list (ItlIwx.cpp:13693-13700): IEEE80211_C_WEP | C_RSN | ... no IEEE80211_C_MFP. Consequently ieee80211_add_rsn_body never sets MFPC/MFPR in assoc RSN IEs (output.c:1082-1086); ieee80211_choose_rsnparams never sets NODE_MFP (node.c:1630-1633); the SA-Query machinery (output.c:1901-1922, input.c:3414-3480) and BIP IGTK handling (pae_input.c:471-474, 641-658 - IGTK KDE only parsed if NODE_MFP; crypto_bip.c entire file) are unreachable. WCL setCIPHER_KEY has no IGTK/BIP case at all (SkywalkInterface.cpp:372-406 - only NONE/WEP/TKIP/AES_CCM/PMK/MSK/PMKSA).
findings.analysis: PMF-required networks refuse association. On PMF-optional networks the client remains exposed to unicast deauth/disassoc spoofing - a standard 802.11w threat, relevant on enterprise/campus APs that enable PMF-capable. No throughput impact.
findings.runtime_confirmation: Kit open question 4: PMF-optional enterprise AP test (does association complete; expected failure only on PMF-required).

findings.title: CCMP core (SW + HW-offload paths) is correct - per-TID replay counters, 11w AAD rules, KRACK guards
findings.evidence: ieee80211_crypto_ccmp.c:93-176 phase1 AAD construction (masks subtype for 11w data, Retry/PS/MoreData, Order for QoS; nonce carries TID + mgmt bit); PN extraction & per-TID RSC selection ieee80211_ccmp_get_pn 322-359 (*prsc = &k->k_rsc[tid], mgmt uses k_mgmt_rsc); replay discard pn <= *prsc (396-401) with MIC check before RSC update (499-507). HW-offload path ieee80211_input_hwdecrypt (input.c:168-261) reuses the same counters with RXI_HWDEC_SAME_PN allowing equal PN across A-MSDU subframes. HAL-side iwx_detect_duplicate + iwx_ccmp_decap (ItlIwx.cpp:5247-5303) implement the same per-TID rule pre-reorder. KRACK protections: NODE_RSN_NEW_PTK gate (pae_input.c:556-599) and must_update_group_key (366-373) prevent key/counter reinstall.
findings.analysis: The primary data-confidentiality engine is the well-audited OpenBSD implementation; no defect found. [severity defaulted]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a.

findings.title: Non-CCMP ciphers run in software on the command gate; TKIP countermeasures are a no-op
findings.evidence: iwx_set_key (ItlIwx.cpp:10060-10062): 'Fallback to software crypto for other ciphers'; iwx_tx (7073-7086): non-CCMP frames are ieee80211_encrypt()-ed in software then flagged IWX_TX_FLAGS_ENCRYPT_DIS. TKIP Michael-MIC failure countermeasures explicitly stubbed: ieee80211_encap output.c:623-625 if ((ic_flags & F_COUNTERM) && ni_rsncipher == TKIP) /* XXX TKIP countermeasures! */; and the MIC-failure timeout is hostap-only (crypto.c:84-87).
findings.analysis: On TKIP networks every frame is RC4+Michael'd on the single workloop gate - throughput collapses to low-tens Mbps and CPU burns; MIC-failure storms (active attack or noisy link) can never trigger the mandated 60-second shutdown, leaving a legacy network attackable. WPA/WPA2-CCMP (the common case) unaffected. [report: CONFIRMED DEFECT (performance no-op part) + UNSUPPORTED (SW crypto part)]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a - TKIP-network throughput test if such an AP is available.

findings.title: Host rate adaptation (MiRA + AMRR + rssadapt) is dead code; firmware TLC is the sole rate controller
findings.evidence: No caller of ieee80211_ra_add_stats_ht/ra_choose/ra_node_init exists in ItlIwx.cpp (repo-wide search: only definitions in itl80211/). Rate flow: iwx_rs_init sends TLC_MNG_CONFIG_CMD (ItlIwx.cpp:9375-9434, HE mode for AX211, per-BW rate masks 9211-9270); firmware reports decisions via TLC_MNG_UPDATE_NOTIF -> iwx_rs_update (9574-9631) which merely records ni_txmcs/ni_txrate/ni_he_txrate_kbps for status; iwx_tx_fill_cmd (6885-6887) uses ni_txmcs only as an initial-rate seed without CMD_RATE. TX status retry counters parsed but only printed (iwx_rx_tx_cmd 6176-6187 DPRINTFN; rx_tx_cmd_single 5988-6008 just bumps outputErrors). Risk residue: ieee80211_ra_get_rateset ends in panic (ra.c:278); no host watchdog on rate state.
findings.analysis: Consistent with the prior audit (gen3 firmware TLC). Hazards: any future caller wiring MiRA back in can kernel-panic; if the firmware TLC stalls (e.g. after the DRV-IWX-011 queue freeze) there is no host watchdog on rate state. [report: VALIDATED (fw owns rates) with UNVERIFIED (dead-code hazards)]
findings.runtime_confirmation: Kit open question 2: check iwx_rs_update 'new rate:' log lines after stall episodes.

findings.title: TX aggregation enable is slow and fragile - 1 s initial delay, 30 s backoff, open networks never aggregate
findings.evidence: Chain of gates before a frame rides an A-MPDU: (1) ieee80211_encap output.c:629-646 - only QoS-eligible data frames (not EAPOL) with ba_state != AGREED call node_trigger_addba_req; caps check (ic_caps & C_TX_AMPDU_SETUP_IN_RS) == 0 (640) - IWX never sets _IN_RS, so the net80211 timer path is active even though the driver also sets _IN_HW. (2) trigger_addba_req arms ni_addba_req_to[tid] at ni_addba_req_intval[tid] - initialized to 1 s (node.c:1762-1763), backoff doubling to 30 s max on each failure (ADDBA_REQ_INTVAL_MAX, node.h:439; incremented in recv_addba_resp input.c:3272-3274 and tx_ba_timeout proto.c:1062-1064). (3) addba_request -> iwx_ampdu_tx_start returns EBUSY -> iwx_ba_task (4604-4636) allocates the TVQM queue and calls addba_resp_accept immediately - the firmware runs the actual ADDBA exchange. (4) Aggregation additionally forbidden on open networks: can_use_ampdu requires F_RSNON && PROTO_RSN (output.c:490-507, deliberate anti-injection policy).
findings.analysis: Every association/reassociation pays >=1 s of non-aggregated legacy-framed TX before A-MPDU starts; after a failed ADDBA the TID can wait up to 30 s. Combined with DRV-11D-011 (non-aggregated frames not even QoS-marked) the post-roam throughput ramp is minutes-scale worst case. On open/guest SSIDs throughput is permanently capped at legacy non-aggregated levels.
findings.runtime_confirmation: Kit: throughput ramp measurement right after join (speed test timing); watch ADDBA timing in 08-kernel-log.

findings.title: BA teardown on roam/deauth leaks the RX reorder buffers and any mbufs inside them
findings.evidence: ieee80211_ba_del (node.c:2029-2051) resets ba_state and cancels timers but never frees ba->ba_buf (allocated in recv_addba_req, input.c:3155-3159, malloc(64 x sizeof(struct ieee80211_ba_buf)) per TID) and never frees mbufs parked in the window. node_cleanup (node.c:1660-1686) and node_copy (1695-1713) call only ba_del/ba_free (timeout_free only). Every roam executes this via join_bss -> ic_node_copy (node.c:1255) and every deauth via newstate cleanup. Verified against upstream itlwm (git show 7204c69) - inherited divergence; current OpenBSD frees the buffer here.
findings.analysis: Leak rate ~ up to 8 TIDs x ~2 KB + up to 64 held mbufs per roam. On a machine that roams frequently (weak RF, bgscan auto-roam enabled) this is a slow kernel-memory/mbuf leak -> prolonged uptime degradation, contributing to 'wider unreliability'. Cleanly torn-down sessions (DELBA path, input.c:3382-3389) do free correctly.
findings.runtime_confirmation: Kit open question 1: log capture across >=20 forced roams watching vm_page/mbuf pressure from reorder-buffer leaks.

findings.title: Roam/deauth tears TX BA down silently - no DELBA to the AP, no driver notification from net80211
findings.evidence: iwx_rm_sta (ItlIwx.cpp:7647-7678) loops agreed TX BAs with ieee80211_delba_request(ic, ni, /*reason=*/0, 1, i) - reason 0 means no DELBA frame is transmitted (proto.c:1161-1165). net80211's own ba_del (node.c:2044-2051) never calls ic_ampdu_tx_stop either. The only path that would release the HAL TVQM queue, iwx_ampdu_tx_stop (ItlIwx.cpp:4714-4729), merely sets sc_tid_data[tid].qid = IWX_INVALID_QUEUE - it never frees the queue (DRV-IWX-011) and early-returns if ba_state != AGREED.
findings.analysis: After each roam the AP-side BA state is stale until it times out, and the driver-side aggregation queue leaks (prior audit). Sequence restart at the new AP starts from ba_winstart of the freshly allocated queue (ba_task 4620-4621). Net effect: repeated roams accumulate leaked queues until iwx_tvqm_alloc_txq fails -> aggregation permanently refused (addba_resp_refuse 4632) -> throughput pinned at legacy rates until reboot. Strongest systemic explanation candidate for progressive degradation. [severity and confidence normalized from Medium-High]
findings.runtime_confirmation: Kit open question 1: 'Failed allocating TXQ' after >=20 roams; ADDBA refusals in 08-kernel-log.

findings.title: Non-aggregated TX frames are sent without QoS headers; per-AC scheduling does not exist
findings.evidence: ieee80211_encap output.c:636-646: 'We use QoS data frames for aggregation only.' - before BA AGREED, frames get a plain ieee80211_frame header and sequence numbers from the shared non-QoS counter ni->ni_txseq (684-686); after agreement, per-TID ni_qos_txseqs[tid] (680-682). _iwx_start_task (ItlIwx.cpp:10850) int ac = EDCA_AC_BE /* XXX */, ifq is FIFO (ifq_dequeue 10884), and ieee80211_classify's DSCP->UP result is used only for the TID field. All non-aggregated traffic (including EAPOL and all management) shares the single non-aggregation TX ring (iwx_tx 6996-7014, qid = first_data_qid).
findings.analysis: Pre-ADDBA and EAPOL frames cannot use WMM priority at all, and any AC differentiation only exists once per-TID aggregation queues are up. A bulk BE/BK burst on the shared ring can delay VO/mgmt/EAPOL - handshake frames time out (100 ms EAPOL timeout, pae_output.c:139) and the association restarts. Amplifies DRV-IWX-010. [report: by design upstream, but consequential here]
findings.runtime_confirmation: Kit open question 6: bulk TCP during (re)association - measure whether 4-way msg2/4 (100 ms timeout) get delayed on the shared ring enough to force re-auth loops.

findings.title: EAPOL is consumed by the in-driver supplicant under WCL; never forwarded to macOS on PSK networks
findings.evidence: input.c:1136-1155: under AIRPORT_WCL, an EAPOL frame is duplicated to the stack only if (ic->ic_wcl_enterprise); the original always goes to ieee80211_eapol_key_input - the OpenBSD supplicant, which performs the 4-way handshake (msg2/msg4 via send_eapol_key, pae_output.c:75-148, queued on if_snd) and installs PTK/GTK through ic_set_key (pae_input.c:587, 629). ic_wcl_enterprise is set only by WCL join requests (WCL.cpp:453) and cleared on stop/join paths (533, 576, 610, 679). PSK injected via setASSOCIATION -> ic_psk (SkywalkInterface.cpp:151-153).
findings.analysis: Works, but macOS's own supplicant is bypassed for PSK; any macOS-side diagnostic/roaming logic that expects to see EAPOL sees nothing. Combined with DRV-11D-011 (EAPOL on the congested shared ring at legacy framing), handshakes under load are the fragile point. [severity normalized from Info/Low]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a.

findings.title: TX BA sessions have no inactivity timeout - ba_timeout_val forced to 0
findings.evidence: ieee80211_addba_request (proto.c:1119) ba->ba_timeout_val = 0; and iwx_ba_task (ItlIwx.cpp:4622) ba->ba_timeout_val = 0. Both ieee80211_input_ba (input.c:847-848) and ieee80211_addba_resp_accept (input.c:3319-3320) only arm the inactivity timer if (ba->ba_timeout_val != 0). ADDBA requests therefore advertise a timeout value of 0 ('no timeout') to the AP.
findings.analysis: Stale TX BA state persists until DELBA/roam; a queue that wedges (DRV-IWX-011) is never reaped by inactivity. Conversely RX-side timeouts use the AP-provided value and work. [report: lifecycle gap; severity normalized from Low-Medium]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a.

findings.title: RX A-MSDU/A-MPDU deaggregation, reordering and duplicate/replay detection validated correct
findings.evidence: A-MSDU: ieee80211_amsdu_decap (input.c:1270-1362) - 3-byte pad handling (1354-1355), subframe length checks (1298-1330), FragAttacks mitigations amsdu_decap_validate (1223-1265, LLC-header-MAC blackhole, STA DA==self). Reorder: ieee80211_input_ba (832-916) with window slide/jump heuristics (ba_winmiss <= 8, stats counters), input_ba_seq/flush/gap_skip (922-1030), gap timeout 300 ms (BA_GAP_TIMEOUT, node.h:289). Fragments dropped entirely (input.c:399-411, citing vanhoef usenix2021) - defrag code #ifdef notyet (736-826). Duplicate detection per-TID ni_qos_rxseqs with RXI_SAME_SEQ for fw-deaggregated subframes (input.c:413-435) plus HAL-side iwx_detect_duplicate (ItlIwx.cpp:5454-5477) which understands A-MSDU subframe indices.
findings.analysis: No defect found in the deaggregation/reorder engine (the net80211 layer is only in the loop for non-fw-reordered frames on this gen3 hardware - firmware reorder short-circuits with RXI_AMPDU_DONE). [severity defaulted]
findings.runtime_confirmation: n/a.

findings.title: No station power-save at the 802.11 layer: no PS bit, no TIM decode for own AID, no PS-Poll; PS fully delegated to firmware
findings.evidence: TX frames never set IEEE80211_FC1_PWR_MGT (grep across output.c/pae_output.c - zero hits; the only PS-bit code is hostap RX handling input.c:453-481 and ieee80211_pwrsave for AP buffering output.c:2275-2322, both STA_ONLY-compiled-out). Beacon TIM parsing extracts only dtim_count/dtim_period (input.c:1820-1825) to feed ic_updatedtim -> iwx_updatedtim (ItlIwx.cpp:4539-4547, re-sends MAC context). PS-Poll is hostap-only (recv_pspoll input.c:3583+, #ifndef STA_ONLY). Firmware PS: iwx_power_build_cmd (7363-7391) sets only POWER_SAVE_ENA (no POWER_MANAGEMENT_ENA -> ba_enable=0, beacon-abort off), keep-alive >= 3xDTIM; iwx_power_update_device (7414-7426) always enables device PS when not monitor.
findings.analysis: net80211's own PS machinery is intentionally inert; all AP-buffering behavior is firmware LAR/MVM PS. U-APSD absent (DRV-IWX-016) - APs see a non-U-APSD STA and buffer/queue accordingly. Multicast/DTIM delivery depends entirely on fw keep-alive; user-visible risk is delayed IPv6 SLAAC/ND multicast during doze. [report: by delegation]
findings.runtime_confirmation: Kit 09-power; IPv6 SLAAC/ND latency after wake.

findings.title: Regulatory: LAR/firmware MCC with NVM channel tables; DFS passive-only in WCL scans; a global PRE_SCAN_PASSIVE2ACTIVE flag is a compliance question mark
findings.evidence: Channels from NVM iwx_init_channel_map (ItlIwx.cpp:3894-3992) - CHAN_PASSIVE when !NVM_CHANNEL_ACTIVE (3951-3952), CHAN_DFS (3981-3983); LAR init iwx_send_update_mcc_cmd(sc, ZZ) (10691-10698) and geo-located country updates (WCL deferWCLCountryUpdate -> MCC_UPDATE_CMD, WCL.cpp:28-64, ItlIwx.cpp:10498-10558, refreshed channel map 8523-8537). WCL active-probe decision excludes DFS/passive: probeChannel = active && !passiveOnly && !dfs (WCL.hpp:426-428). However iwx_config_umac_scan sets global scan_config->channel_flags |= IWX_CHANNEL_FLAG_PRE_SCAN_PASSIVE2ACTIVE (ItlIwx.cpp:7963-7966).
findings.analysis: DFS channels are not actively probed by host decision (good), but the passive2active flag invites the firmware to convert passive channels to active after the first scan - if that applies to DFS channels in ETSI domains this is a regulatory exposure needing fw-behavior confirmation. regdomain.c is only a name<->code mapping table (2015 vintage); actual rules live in firmware geo profiles; no host-side CAC/radar handling exists (fine for STA; DFS-master impossible anyway). [report: UNVERIFIED (flag) + VALIDATED (DFS); severity normalized from Low-Medium]
findings.runtime_confirmation: Kit open question 3: sniffer capture on a DFS channel or fw-behavior confirmation.

findings.title: Roaming is always full AUTH + 4-way handshake - no 802.11r/FT, no fast path
findings.evidence: No MDIE/FTIE/FT AKM handling anywhere (rg for 11r/FT/MDIE/fast transition -> nothing in net80211 or WCL); roam path node_switch_bss/join_bss (node.c:1192-1321) always transitions to S_AUTH (1319) and re-runs the full handshake. PMKID caching exists (choose_rsnparams node.c:1612-1618, PMKSA cache crypto.c:643-695, pmk_lifetime /* XXX not used yet */ at 664) which skips 802.1X but never the 4-way.
findings.analysis: Every roam costs auth + assoc + EAPOL 4-way (~100-400 ms typical, worse if EAPOL starves per DRV-11D-011/012), then >= 1 s aggregation ramp (DRV-11D-008). This chain is the per-roam 'burst of unusability' users experience. [report severity: roam latency]
